name: vegaduta-vscode
description: Free AI coding help that runs on your own machine - chat, inline completions, Explain/Fix/Refactor, code review, commit messages and a coding agent - with no account and no quota. Sign in to add your VegaDuta workspace's hosted agents and workflows.

commands.title: Use API Key (vmcp_) Instead of Signing In

vegaduta.environment.description: Which VegaDuta deployment to talk to.

vegaduta.customApiBase.description: API origin for the custom environment, e.g. https://api.example.com. Used only when vegaduta.environment is "custom".

vegaduta.customAuthBase.description: Keycloak origin for the custom environment, e.g. https://auth.example.com. Used only when vegaduta.environment is "custom".

vegaduta.completions.provider.description: Inline completion source. auto = the on-device engine when one is ready (a downloaded WebLLM model or a local Ollama-compatible server), otherwise the platform; local = on-device only; hosted = the platform's fill-in-the-middle endpoint, metered under your tenant budget (needs sign-in); off = disabled.

vegaduta.edge.enabled.description: Allow the chat view to start the on-device engine for chat, completions and quick actions. Two backends: a WebLLM model running on your GPU inside the panel (download it from the panel's engine chip or "VegaDuta: Download an On-Device Model"; nothing downloads by itself), and an OpenAI-compatible server you run (Ollama / LM Studio / llama.cpp) at vegaduta.ollama.baseUrl.

vegaduta.ollama.baseUrl.description: Origin of your local OpenAI-compatible server for on-device chat, completions and quick actions. Empty = http://127.0.0.1:11434 (Ollama's default). LM Studio is usually http://127.0.0.1:1234. Applied the next time the chat view opens.

vegaduta.agent.baseUrl.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint the coding agent talks to. Empty = auto-discovery: whichever local server is actually running on 127.0.0.1 (Ollama 11434, LM Studio 1234, llama.cpp 8080), found once per session and needing no key. Set it to a provider origin (e.g. https://api.groq.com/openai) to use your own key instead. "VegaDuta: Set Up the Coding Agent" reports what discovery found.

vegaduta.agent.model.description: Model id for the coding agent. Empty = the first model the server lists whose name is known to call tools, else the server's first model. It MUST support tool calling - qwen2.5-coder, llama3.1, mistral-nemo and devstral do.

vegaduta.agent.maxSteps.description: Hard ceiling on agent loop iterations for one task. A bound is a safety property, not a tuning knob - raise it deliberately.

vegaduta.agent.autoApproveEdits.description: Apply the agent's file edits without asking each time. Off by default: this extension will not edit your files unattended unless you say so.

vegaduta.agent.autoApproveCommands.description: Run the agent's shell commands without asking each time. Off by default. Turning this on lets a model run arbitrary commands on your machine.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with VegaDuta
walkthroughs.description: Free on-device AI in two clicks, reviews and commit messages, the coding agent, then your workspace's agents.

steps.title: Run a model on your machine
steps.description:
Open the VegaDuta panel and click the engine chip to download a small model that runs on your GPU. Chat, Explain/Fix/Refactor and inline completions then work with no account and nothing sent anywhere.
[Download an On-Device Model](command:vegaduta.downloadModel)

steps.title: Review changes and write commit messages
steps.description:
Get a review of your uncommitted changes, a drafted commit message in the Source Control box (you still commit), and a plain-language explanation of any error from its lightbulb.
[Review My Changes](command:vegaduta.reviewChanges)

steps.title: Set up the coding agent
steps.description:
A multi-step agent that reads, searches, edits and runs commands in this workspace against a local server (Ollama / LM Studio) or your own API key. Every edit shows a diff first; every command asks.
[Set Up the Coding Agent](command:vegaduta.setUpCodingAgent)

steps.title: Turn on inline completions
steps.description:
Fill-in-the-middle suggestions in every language, from the on-device engine when it is ready or the platform when you are signed in.
[Toggle Inline Completions](command:vegaduta.toggleCompletions)

steps.title: Use the Toolkit, or go private
steps.description:
Ready-made recipes for your role - developer, tester, reviewer, architect, product/BA or DevOps - plus Code Tour, Rubber Duck, Second Opinion, Ask the team and Machine Check in the panel. Private Mode keeps every prompt, file and search query on this machine; VS Code enforces it too.
[Toggle Private Mode](command:vegaduta.togglePrivateMode)

steps.title: Sign in for your tenant's agents (optional)
steps.description:
Chat with the agents and run the workflows your VegaDuta tenant already has. Uses the OAuth device flow, so it works over Remote/SSH/WSL.
[Sign In](command:vegaduta.signIn)

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The coding agent runs commands and edits files. In an untrusted folder it stays off, and the agent settings are machine-scoped so a repository cannot enable it, redirect the model endpoint, or disable the approval prompts.
